title: Reliability Caps
description:
Research code for measuring what a single human observation is worth to a spatial decision, given a learned partition of the landscape.

A settlement is partitioned into parts by clustering a satellite representation. A resident's report is about the cell they stand in, the decision is about the whole part, and composing those two stages bounds the evidence one report can carry at log(TPR/FPR) nats, where TPR and FPR are the out-of-sample reliability of the partition itself. Evidence then accumulates towards an escalation boundary and decays at the hazard's own autocorrelation time, which turns that bound into a condition on whether a part can be decided at all.

This deposit holds the evidence core, thirteen experiments and the results of the runs behind them: the TESSERA and Copernicus GLO-30 processing, the eight-settlement comparison, a Sentinel-1 detectability test, a hand-built Sentinel-2 composite baseline, and the granularity and alpha-margin sweeps. The results are included as JSON alongside the configuration that produced each one, so any number can be checked without repeating an hour of computation.

No third-party data is redistributed. Every script fetches what it needs from the public archives and caches locally.
